extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of literature, poets, literary critics, and philosophers
extracted.subtask_description: Philosophical guidance on imagination, mind, and moral sentiment as they relate to poetry and the formation/evaluation of ideas; aimed at informing poets, critics, and students about how imagination and moral feeling should be cultivated and understood. Emphasises grounding poetic invention in perception, the unity of ideas, and the moral purpose of benevolence and justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception as basis of thought
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is an axiom in mental philosophy, that we can think of nothing which we have not perceived."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thought, imagination, reasoning and memory must be ultimately derived from perception; poetic invention is a recombination of sensations. Use perceptions as the raw material of thought and poetry rather than conjuring wholly non-sensory ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry as combination of sensations
rubrics_metrics.description: "The most astonishing combinations of poetry, the subtlest deductions of logic and mathematics, are no other than combinations which the intellect makes of sensations according to its own laws."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate poetic excellence by the skillful combination of sensory impressions according to intellectual laws; strong poetry rearranges and recombines perceptions into new, expressive wholes.

rubrics_metrics.name: No essential distinction between kinds of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Thoughts, or ideas, or notions, differ from each other, not in kind, but in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid rigidly separating 'real' (external) ideas from dreams, hallucinations, or mad ideas when considering imaginative material; treat all ideas as the same kind differing in intensity, duration, connexion, recurrence and utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure ideas by intensity and relations
rubrics_metrics.description: A scale might be formed, graduated according to the degrees of a combined ratio of intensity, duration, connexion, periods of recurrence, and utility, which would be the standard, according to which all ideas might be measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging or crafting ideas (poetic or philosophical), consider their strength along dimensions like intensity, duration, connectivity, recurrence and usefulness; these varied measures form a graduated standard of value among ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogy as foundation for inferring other minds
rubrics_metrics.description: The basis of this relation [evidence of other minds] is, undoubtedly, a periodical recurrence of masses of ideas... The law, according to which these deductions are drawn, is called analogy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that belief about others and broader imaginative inference is based on analogous patterns in experience; poetic empathy and depiction of minds rely on analogy grounded in recurring ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider mind and universe as a whole
rubrics_metrics.description: He is not a moral, and an intellectual,--but also, and pre-eminently, an imaginative being. ... we ought to consider the mind of man and the universe as the great whole on which to exercise our speculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid fragmentary approaches; in metaphysical or poetic inquiry, treat the mind and the universe synthetically. This wholistic stance discourages hair-splitting verbal disputes and encourages expansive imaginative synthesis in art and philosophy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground metaphysics in incontestable inner facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Metaphysics will thus possess this conspicuous advantage ... that each student, by attentively referring to his own mind, may ascertain the authorities upon which any assertions regarding it are supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When theorizing about the mind or composing introspective poetry, base claims on observable, first-person mental facts accessible to any attentive student; prefer introspective evidence over abstract speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-detailed, circumscribed analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Most of the errors of philosophers have arisen from considering the human being in a point of view too detailed and circumscribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses that isolate the mind into narrow categories lead to error; prefer broader imaginative and synthetic perspectives when evaluating or producing work about human nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: On method: set aside verbal disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Here, above all, verbal disputes ought to be laid aside, though this has long been their chosen field of battle. It imports little to inquire whether thought be distinct from the objects of thought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In philosophical-poetic practice, avoid getting bogged down in semantics (internal/external distinctions); focus on phenomena and their imaginative or moral significance instead of word-games.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution in generalizing from particular introspections
rubrics_metrics.description: I shall employ caution, indeed, as to the facts which I state, that they contain nothing false or exaggerated. But they contain no more than certain elucidations of my own nature; concerning the degree in which it resembles, or differs from, that of others, I am by no means accurately aware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using personal dreams, memories or introspective incidents as evidence or poetic material, be wary of over-generalizing from singular cases; indicate limits and avoid claiming undue universality from private experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dream-phenomena as distinct associative material
rubrics_metrics.description: In dreams, images acquire associations peculiar to dreaming; ... the idea of a particular house, when it recurs a second time in dreams, will have relation with the idea of the same house, in the first time, of a nature entirely different from that which the house excites, when seen or thought of in relation to waking ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat dream-images as having their own associative logic distinct from waking perception; poets may exploit these altered associations, but should be attentive to their differing coherence and resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtue defined by greatest happiness principle
rubrics_metrics.description: It is admitted that a virtuous or moral action, is that action which, when considered in all its accessories and consequences, is fitted to produce the highest pleasure to the greatest number of sensitive beings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When discussing moral themes in literature or moral evaluation, use the utilitarian-style yardstick: actions judged by their tendency to maximize net pleasure across sentient beings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtue consists of benevolence and justice
rubrics_metrics.description: The disposition in an individual to promote this object is called virtue; and the two constituent parts of virtue, benevolence and justice, are correlative with these two great portions of the only true object of all voluntary actions of a human being.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral character (in depiction or normative evaluation) should be assessed in terms of benevolence (desire to produce good) and justice (apprehension of how good ought to be done); both components are required for full virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate imagination to produce benevolence
rubrics_metrics.description: The only distinction between the selfish man and the virtuous man is, that the imagination of the former is confined within a narrow limit, whilst that of the latter embraces a comprehensive circumference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To foster moral sentiment and sympathetic depiction in writing, cultivate the imagination through exposure to poetry, philosophy and refined thought; a wide imagination expands sympathy and benevolence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice moderates benevolence; equal distribution principle
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a sentiment in the human mind that regulates benevolence in its application as a principle of action. This is the sense of justice. ... If ten men are shipwrecked on a desert island, they distribute whatever subsistence may remain to them, into equal portions among themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When representing moral choices or framing moral argument in art, acknowledge that benevolence must be guided by justice—fairness in distribution and consideration of claims—not mere indiscriminate compassion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject virtue grounded solely in external penalties or rewards
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtue is a law, to which it is the will of the lawgiver that we should conform; which will we should in no manner be bound to obey, unless some dreadful punishment were attached to disobedience. This is the philosophy of slavery and superstition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral worth in action derives from internal motive (desire to do good), not from obedience produced by threat of punishment or promise of reward; in moral criticism or characterisation, distinguish genuine virtue from coerced conformity.
